decisions.reason: The source adds a light-sensor I2C connector to the integrated-board variant, not to the separate sensor-board connector hub.
Adding a light-sensor connector for the backlight does not change the e-paper backlight's electrical supply, switching, PWM, or light-source requirements.
The source specifies an I2C connector but provides no logic-voltage information and does not change the existing sensor level-shifting policy.
The newly included light-sensor I2C connection is unrelated to the SPS30 SEL-to-GND configuration and I2C operating mode.
The light-sensor I2C connector does not alter the panel reset connector or its EN-to-GND behavior.
The source adds a distinct I2C light-sensor interface and does not modify the PIR input connector.
The added light-sensor I2C connector does not affect the panel buttons, slide switch, GPIO assignments, or connector mounting.
The source does not change either TTP223 touch interface, its connector, or its GPIO assignment.
A light sensor intended for backlight use is electrically and functionally distinct from the addressable LED power and data interface.
The source concerns an integrated-board light-sensor connector and does not modify the separate eight-LED array board.
The light-sensor I2C addition has no effect on the passive buzzer selection or interface.
The source refines the integrated board's sensor connector matrix without changing the established single-board architecture, interboard-connector policy, or cost-reduction goal.
